title: Grades 3–5 Mini Test — Writing: Cooking with Family
overview: A short writing practice. First, build a paragraph and fix verbs. Then write a story from pictures and explain a food you would share.

sections.title: Part 1: Build Sentences
sections.directions: Put the sentences in order. Then choose the right word for each blank.

items.title: Build the Paragraph
items.prompt: Put the sentences in order to make a paragraph about making tortillas.

items.text: Next, we rolled the dough into small balls and pressed them flat.
Last Sunday, I made tortillas with my grandmother.
Finally, we cooked them in a hot pan and ate them with our family.
First, we mixed flour, water, and a little salt in a big bowl.

vocabulary: words that tell when something happens
palabras de orden: palabras que dicen cuándo pasa algo
a group of sentences about one idea
párrafo: un grupo de oraciones sobre una idea
items.correct: Correct. The paragraph starts by telling when and who, then follows first, next, and finally.
items.hint: Find the sentence that tells when the story happened. It goes first.
items.support: Order words help: first, next, finally.

items.title: Past-Tense Verbs
items.prompt: Choose the word that correctly finishes each sentence.
items.correct: Correct. The word "yesterday" tells us to use past-tense verbs: cooked, washed, set.
items.hint: The word "yesterday" means the story already happened.
items.support: Many past-tense verbs end in -ed. "Set" stays the same.

sections.title: Part 2: Write Your Own
sections.directions: Read each task. Look at the picture if there is one. Plan your ideas, then write in complete sentences. Use the word bank and sentence frames. Check your writing when you finish.

items.title: Making Tortillas
items.prompt: Look at the three pictures. Write a story about the girl and her grandmother. Tell what they did first, next, and last. Write 3 to 5 sentences.
writeFor: one sentence or more for each picture

models.A: Girl and grandma. Mix. Roll. Eat tortillas.
models.B: First, the girl and her grandma mixed dough in a bowl. Next, they rolled the dough flat. Finally, the family ate tortillas together.
models.C: First, Valeria and her grandmother mixed flour and water in a big blue bowl to make dough. Next, they rolled the dough into little balls and pressed them flat with a rolling pin. Finally, the whole family sat at the table and ate a big stack of tortillas. Valeria felt proud because she helped make dinner.

items.correct: Strong response (model): First, Valeria and her grandmother mixed flour and water in a big blue bowl to make dough. Next, they rolled the dough into little balls and pressed them flat with a rolling pin. Finally, the whole family sat at the table and ate a big stack of tortillas. Valeria felt proud because she helped make dinner.
items.hint: Write about each picture in order. Give the girl a name.
items.support: Use the word bank and the sentence frames. Read your writing again when you finish and fix one thing.

picture.alt: Three pictures in order. 1: A girl and her grandmother mix dough with a spoon in a big bowl next to a bag of flour. 2: They roll the dough into balls and flatten them into thin circles with a rolling pin. 3: The family sits at the table and shares a big stack of tortillas together.

items.title: A Food to Share
items.prompt: What food from your family or culture would you like to share with your class? Tell what it is, how it tastes, and why you would share it. Write 4 to 6 sentences.

models.B: I would share jollof rice with my class. It is made with rice and tomatoes. It tastes a little spicy. I would share it because my family eats it on holidays.
models.C: I would like to share pupusas with my class. They are thick corn tortillas filled with cheese and beans, and they taste warm and soft. My grandmother makes them every Saturday, and the whole family helps. I would share them because they remind me of El Salvador, and I want my friends to learn about my culture. I think everyone would want a second one!

items.correct: Strong response (model): I would like to share pupusas with my class. They are thick corn tortillas filled with cheese and beans, and they taste warm and soft. My grandmother makes them every Saturday, and the whole family helps. I would share them because they remind me of El Salvador, and I want my friends to learn about my culture. I think everyone would want a second one!
items.hint: Tell what the food is first. Then describe it and give a reason.
items.support: Use the word bank and the sentence frames. Read your writing again when you finish and fix one thing.
